Pilot re: Bangladesh/Burma
April 20, 2023
(SBU) Draft Agenda
(SBU, Engagement Framework
Attendees from USAID:
• DRG: Vera Zakem
• ITR/DRG: Garth Willis
• CPS: Amy Malessa
• Asia Bureau: ?
Other USG Attendees:
• State Department and National Security Council
Background from State Department, USAID and National Security Council:
• Recapped the same toplines from Meta call
• Importance of proactive approach to violence and atrocity prevention, intersects with human
rights and information integrity
• Importance of empowering USAID staff and partners on-the-ground to prevent and respond to
violence
• WH emphasized that State/USAID will take the lead on this initiative moving forward - the goal is
to make these engagements more intentional and consistent
• Hope to consolidate our response across the USG so that RFls/asks do not fall through the cracks
moving forward
• Will start with Burma and then move into Bangladesh as pilots - political toplines provided on
the context from unclassified reporting
Presentation from YouTube - "How YouTube Works: Key Events Initiative" (see slides):
• Government and Public Affairs Team across Google / YouTube - whole team dedicated to foreign
affairs and national security, including staff dedicated to Asia Pacific
• YouTube provided toplines on the penetration of YouTube services - number of videos, channels,
etc.
• YouTube has global, guiding principles (e.g. Community Guidelines) to remove, raise, and reward
users
• YouTube has content moderation standards - apply equally to all speakers, in all languages, at all
times
• Trust and Safety Teams across the globe - locations of staffing not disclosed
• YouTube has a variety of policies to prevent offline harm...

• YouTube is launched in Bangladesh, YouTube Partnership Program is operational (can monetize
content)

• YouTube has local language UX/UI available in Bangladesh, including a dedicated a local Trust
and Safety Team
• YouTube has quarterly meetings with regulator in Bangladesh
• YouTube has rolled out their Trusted Flaggers program in Bangladesh as well
• YouTube also has their Threat Analysis Group (TAG) in Bangladesh
• YouTube is talking internally about how to prepare for elections in Bangladesh, Burma, and
Thailand - to help to detect and mitigate threats early
• YouTube has policies related to elections and rule of law - to prevent electoral manipulation and
irregularities
• YouTube puts in place a Watch Desk before an election, surge 3rd party content moderators, and
scrub for the impersonation of politicians
• YouTube will also surge local language capacity six months before an election
• YouTube is not officially launched in Burma - no YouTube Partnership Program (no monetization)
• YouTube recognizes that it is a problem for civil society, journalists, etc. to not be able to
monetize their content in Burma (creators keep the majority of the revenue when monetized)
• YouTube has a light version of YouTube in Burma; Burmese language UX/Ul available, but doesn't
feature local news, sports, creators, etc. - it's bare bones
• But, YouTube does have local language capacity in Burma
• YouTube also has Trusted Flaggers, a dedicated threat escalation channel, and the more official
Threat Analysis Group active in Burma
• YouTube is concerned about channels that havebeen blocked for violating Terms of Service and
are not creating "copycat" channels
• YouTube has a whole system designed to detect - in automated and human ways - users /
content who are trying to get around content removals (e.g. circumvention)
• YouTube is seeing much less content related to the dehumanization of the Rohingya than
hyperbolic pro-Government, pro-authoritarian content
• YouTube does a lot of work around elections - "Global Election Watchers" - includes Google
Search - to help people take part in the democratic process
• YouTube has an election policy related to election results - not miss-stating election results or
claiming victory, etc.
State / USAID Questions and Discussion:
• How does YouTube decide which events require additional resources and/or focus?
• The Intel Team inside YouTube is constantly looking at open source intelligence to
understand and respond to threats, inform YouTube resource decisions
• YouTube had a proactive and thorough approach in Brazil but still couldn't predict the
level of violence
• YouTube has a Major Event Policy - Holocaust, Ukraine, mass/school shootings, etc. -
allows YouTube to remove content that claims the event didn't happen
• Working together the Community Guidelines are flexible enough to respond to
unexpected events
• How quickly can YouTube respond when there are unexpected events?

• On misinformation, there is a Hit Pause Policy - train users on what misinformation is
and how users can respond
• YouTube has Trusted Flaggers - civil society organizations - to help them detect events
quickly, plan in advance, and respond as quick as possible
• What is the process by which YouTube shares threat / intel analysis between platforms? How
can USG align with those efforts?
• Among the industry, there's a lot of sharing between Trust and Safety Teams and the
more centralized Intel Team, Threat Analysis Groups, etc.
• GIFCT is a good example of a consortium that helps to bring together industry partners
to prevent violent extremism / live-streaming of violence
More than 99% of violating / violent content is removed before there are 10 views, but
they are still trying to get better
• YouTube is working on "age-gating" to prevent certain users (under 18 yo) from viewing
violent content
• But, HR defenders will push back because of this is documenting HR violations -
need to make nuanced determinations and responses on violent content
• When do you decide if there's an opportunity to provide in-country training, etc.?
• There is interest by YouTube in providing localized training through Trusted Flaggers, etc.
• Constantly looking for new sources of information to inform their local Trust and Safety
Teams
• How can USAID/State help to make sure the right people are connected on-the-ground?
• Talk to YouTube's local counterparts who cover Burma and Bangladesh - sit in Singapore
and cover Asia Pacific - welcome a follow-up conversation
• Work through Ria / Josh (as "traffic cops") to set-up a deeper dive on both Burma and
Bangladesh
• Would it be helpful to have these conversations more broadly, e.g. with other industry partners?
• More regular touchpoints would be useful - build off initial GEC engagements as a
starting point - good model because it's a regular / standing meeting
It would be useful to have conversations about broad trend lines / threats across all
industry platforms, esp. open source intelligence
• But, it would also be useful to have product / solution-specific conversations by platform
(e.g. concerns related to specific channel / video features, go to YouTube directly)
• Open lines of communication can be just as important or even more important than
resources during times of crisis
• What has YouTube learned about how to detect problematic content over video?
• YouTube is detecting some patterns in video content related to hate speech - uses not
just text, also image detection
• YouTube has a policy related to violent imagery - to detect violent videos that are also
silent
• Age-gating is also used - leaving violent content in a news report as an example but
making it limited by age. We get criticized for leaving this content and for taking down
this content. But it is a way to protect youth, without removing content.

• It's useful for YouTube to have concrete examples (e.g. channels / content) of what State / USAID
finds most problematic, especially from the Field
• For example, YouTube will get examples of VE content from NCTC and will respond to it -
need to be careful this is not construed as USG-requested content removal
• Note: State will look at building out best practices / lessons learned when it comes to engaging
technology companies on these issues. Looking to set up a process for communication,
especially in a crisis situation.
• YouTube agreed that more lines of communication are of course beneficial - suggested
to think about how to do this and highlighted that would be good to have these lines of
communication specific to YouTube as they are a unique platform
